_note: barkhorn's own bought parts, on top of the kit's library (studio/fabkit/library/components.json). From the horn-speaker research of 2026-10-10 (search-result snippets of makers' datasheets and retailer listings; pages could not be opened from this environment): confirm every figure on the datasheet before cutting a baffle. Geometry the datasheets leave out (flange thickness, magnet, roll, cap) is proportioned and marked so.

faital-15pr400-8.model: 15PR400-8 15 in woofer (treated paper cone, neodymium, 8 ohm)
faital-15pr400-8.supplier: Thomann (US storefront; EUR 198 in the EU)
faital-15pr400-8.note: 99 dB 1 W/1 m (Faital); Xmax 5.75 mm ((Hvc - Hg)/2 + Hg/3: winding 15, gap 10.5), Xdamage 15.5; Bl 16.7 T m, Mms 85.2 g; minimum impedance 5.9 ohm; 3.7 L displaced; AES 400 W, 800 W maximum. Round 36: checked against FaitalPRO's current 8 ohm datasheet (printed 2026-10-22): Vas 248.9 L (223 before, an older sheet's), Sd 857 cm2 (805), Le 0.72 mH (0.75), the bolt circle 374 (375); bought from Thomann (thomannmusic.com/faitalpro_15pr400_8_ohms.htm)

geom._coil: the voice coil 77 across (FaitalPRO's drawing, item 16, 2026-11-09); before, the model drew 56 (the default, 0.45 x the magnet)
geom._proportioned: flange_t, surround_w, roll_h, roll_seat (the roll's top level with the flange, as a pro woofer's: confirm on the driver before a grille is fitted), magnet, cap, bolt circle
geom._round31: as FaitalPRO draws and photographs it (spinoffs/barkhorn/drivers31.md): eight spokes, eight slots 9.5 x 7.4, the surround an accordion of four waves, the basket finned round the motor to 150 across at the back; the screws M6 button heads (ISO 7380, 10.5 x 3.3)

bms-4550-16.model: 4550-16 compression driver, 1 in exit, polyester diaphragm, 16 ohm
bms-4550-16.note: 113 dB 1 W/1 m on a horn; BMS recommends crossing at 800 Hz or above

bc-de1085tn-16.model: DE1085TN 2 in compression driver, titanium diaphragm, 100 mm voice coil, neodymium, 16 ohm (round 5: the owner's bigger throat)
bc-de1085tn-16.supplier: Sonovente (EUR 472 incl. VAT, EUR 393 ex; the snippet does not say which impedance)
bc-de1085tn-16.note: 108 dB 1 W/1 m, that is at 4 V into 16 ohm, so 105 dB at 2.83 V (round 35, the engineering review: B&C's 16 ohm sheet; the 8 ohm is 109 dB at 2.83 V); minimum impedance 11.4 ohm; B&C: cross at 800 Hz or above, 12 dB/oct or steeper; audioXpress bench-tested it on B&C's ME60 horn; the 16 ohm version 3 dB less sensitive a volt, so the FA122's hiss 3 dB lower

geom._proportioned: flange_t, body_d (the 154 x 86 envelope is B&C's)

artofsound-jmlc-400.model: Le Cleac'h round horn, 400 mm mouth, solid beech, 1 in throat (the bought alternative to turning the horn)
artofsound-jmlc-400.note: cut-off, coverage and throat flange not stated: confirm it takes the 4550's 2 x M6 on 76.2

felt-glides.model: Felt glides 30 mm, screw-in, a set of 4

m6-tnut-set.model: M6 x 25 button heads (A2) with M6 T-nuts, a set of 8 (the 15PR400's eight holes on 374)

m6-hf-screws.model: M6 x 25 socket caps with washers (the compression driver to the horn's flange), a pair

attenuator-l-pad.model: The HF channel's L-pad: two aluminium-housed wirewound resistors, 25 W (Vishay Dale RH-25 or Arcol HS25 kind), 6.8 ohm in series and 15 ohm across the driver (about -5.5 dB at 16 ohm; trimmed after the first measurement). In the abnormal case (a full-scale HF sine) they dissipate up to 30.6 W inside the sealed compartment (the engineering audit, 2026-11-01: make/engineering-audit.md), so they are screwed with thermal compound to a 3 mm aluminium plate that is bolted, also on compound, to the inside of the FA122's outer plate, the compartment's heatsink to room air; the plate's place and holes to be agreed with Hypex

bark-sheet.model: Bark for laminating, a square metre: paper birch (Betula papyrifera) sheet from fallen or felled trees, or a smooth-barked gum's shed bark pressed flat (or a UV-printed veneer of it); approve a sample board first

grille-cloth.model: Acoustically transparent speaker cloth (a knit sold for grilles), about 0.6 x 0.95 m a grille, in the finish's colour

grille-magnets.model: The ring's and the disc's magnets: eight 15 x 3 neodymium discs (N42) and four 15 x 3 mild-steel discs, a set: four magnets in the panel and the steel discs in the ring's back hold the ring, four in the disc's frame hold the disc to the same steel (round 13)

post-fixings.model: The posts' fittings (the engineering audit, 2026-11-01: make/engineering-audit.md): four M10 x 1 threaded inserts bonded with epoxy into the horn's pads (12 long), in holes drilled through a jig taken off the top's sockets; at the rear, two sockets knurled to 15 and bonded with epoxy into the top and the pad under it (15 long: a 12 bore 13 deep on a 2 floor; the cable post's floor with a 7 hole, the tie post's with a 6.5); at the front, two keyhole sockets, turned and milled bronze, 30 across and 15 deep, bonded with epoxy through the top into the front panel's top edge (the front posts stand over it): a 15 hole that the front post's foot drops into and a 9 slot 10 long toward the back with a 3 lip over a 15 x 4 undercut, so the foot's turned head (14 across, 4 thick, on an 8 neck) hooks under the lip when the horn slides 10 mm back; a PU washer under each lip stops rattles. With the tie rod in rear post 3 tightened, the horn is held at three points and cannot lift: about 150 N up at a front hook and 90 N on the tie under the stability test's push (est.), against several kN for the bonded fittings. Turned to order, a set of eight
post-fixings.supplier: any lighting hardware supplier or turner

hf-pair.model: HF lead: round silicone-sheathed cable 2 x 0.5 mm2, about 5 across, 1.3 m, ferrules at the pod's end and a two-way lever connector (Wago 221-412 or like) on the driver's own leads, a polarised 2-way connector at the compartment's end

skin-fixings.model: Stainless No. 8 x 25 pan-head screws with washers, for the pressed sheets (through 8 mm holes in the plywood, from inside), a set of 60

grille-pegs.model: Grille pegs and cups, a set of four (push-fit; the cups in 10 mm holes 12 deep in the panel's corners)

hf-mount-screws.model: The 2 in driver's fixings: four M6 x 16 countersunk screws (A2), the driver to its adaptor ring, and four M5 x 16 socket caps with washers, the ring to the brass inserts in the horn's boss, a set

m6-plastic-inserts.model: M6 threaded inserts for plastics (self-tapping, brass) with M6 x 25 button heads (A2), a set of 8 (the 15PR400's eight holes on 374, in the HDPE panel; HDPE will not hold a hammered T-nut)

hdpe-weld-rod.model: HDPE welding rod or extrusion-welder granulate, the panels' own polymer, about 0.4 kg a speaker (the cabinet without wood: corners hot-plate butt welded, the panel, the back and the braces extrusion welded inside)

voile-sleeves.model: Black polyester voile (the owner's working default, 2026-11-01: white glowed through the tinted walls in backlight) (a sheer curtain fabric), about 3 m2 a speaker with its seams, sewn into a sleeve round each batt of the lining, so no fibre reaches the ports or the woofer and the batt's face stays even

lse-tape-dots.model: Double-sided tape made for low-surface-energy plastics (3M's 300LSE adhesive or alike), 20 mm dots, about 60 a speaker: four hold each batt's sleeve flat on the HDPE

vhb-clear-dots.model: Clear acrylic foam tape (3M VHB 4910 or alike), 20 mm dots, about 60 a speaker: on a Cloud cabinet four hold each batt's sleeve flat on the acrylic, all but invisible through it

post-sleeves.model: Polyurethane sleeves 12 x 10 x 13, Shore A 90, a pair: pressed into the rear posts' sockets, they centre the posts and stop them buzzing (the front posts' feet sit in their keyhole sockets on PU washers)

tie-rod-set.model: The horn's tie-down (the engineering audit, 2026-11-01: make/engineering-audit.md): an M6 A2-70 threaded rod about 110 long, a knurled M6 nut with a hex for a key and a washer, inside the pod, tightened to 2 N m (about 1.7 kN of preload, against about 90 N it must hold), and a flanged M6 threaded insert (body 9 x 10) bonded with epoxy in the top's underside. It also locks the horn's 10 mm slide, so the front feet stay hooked. A loose tie nut is the one way the horn could lift: its torque is an FAI item

epdm-gasket.model: EPDM sponge gasket, 3 mm, cut as a frame 15 wide for the amplifier compartment's flange

amp-screws-acrylic.model: The FA122's plate in acrylic: ten M4 brass inserts bonded with epoxy into the back on the plate's ten-hole pattern (five each side; the model's holes were measured off Hypex's drawing, to be confirmed against it at first article (the engineering audit, 2026-11-01: make/engineering-audit.md)), after the last anneal; M4 x 16 black machine screws with nylon shoulder washers, the plate's holes opened to 5.5 so it can slide as it warms (over 315 mm acrylic grows about 0.4 mm more than aluminium for a 25 K rise); 3 mm EPDM tape under the plate. Hypex's self-tapping screws crack acrylic.

earth-bond-kit.model: The amplifier compartment's earth bond (round 35, the engineering review's B3): an M4 stainless stud and nut, a star washer, and a green and yellow lead 1.0 mm2 about 150 long with M4 ring terminals, from a bared spot on the compartment to the FA122's earth point

amp-box-screws.model: Ten screws for the amplifier compartment's flange, with washers: thread-forming screws for plastics (EJOT PT K40 x 12 kind) into HDPE, M4 screws into inserts bonded in acrylic, or wood screws into plywood

cable-glands.model: Three M12 nylon cable glands for 3 to 6.5 mm cable, black: two in the amplifier compartment's front, one under the top at the cable post, in an M12 insert for plastics (in acrylic, a thread tapped in the top)

hf-protect-cap.model: 33 uF 100 V polypropylene film capacitor, in series with the driver (a first-order high-pass at about 300 Hz into 16 ohm), clipped on nylon standoffs 3 mm off the compartment's pan (the engineering audit, 2026-11-01: the L-pad is gone; the HF channel is attenuated in the FA122's DSP)

loom-set.model: The loom: cable-tie bases every 120, with thread-forming screws for plastics (EJOT PT K30 x 10 kind) in HDPE and on bonded M3 brass inserts with M3 screws in acrylic (round 35: nothing self-tapping into acrylic, which cracks round a formed thread), ties, a polarised 2-way connector (Molex Mini-Fit Jr or Wago 2092 kind) for each lead at the compartment, crimped insulated 6.3 mm receptacles at the woofer, silicone sleeving where the HF lead meets the post's cut ends

port-fixings.model: The ports' fixings: eight black countersunk screws, four through each port's frame into the panel (thread-forming screws for plastics, EJOT PT K40 kind, 4 x 16 in the 20 mm HDPE; M4 x 16 into tapped threads in the 20 mm acrylic; wood screws 4 x 14 in the plywood; round 15: their holes stop 2 short of the panel's back), and a 1 mm closed-cell PE foam gasket under each frame

rating-plate.model: Rating plate 70 x 40 x 1, black anodised aluminium, laser-marked: the model, the serial number, the ratings, the WEEE bin and the maker's address (round 35: the CE, UKCA and FCC marks only once the speaker has earned them); two M3 screws into inserts

back-gasket.model: EPDM sponge strip 25 x 3, closed cell, cut and joined as a frame on the back's four land strips, punched for its 16 screws

cap-o-ring.model: O-ring for the horn's cap, 182 x 2 mm, EPDM 70 Shore A (round 16: the twist-lock), and a tube of silicone grease

back-screws.model: M5 button heads (ISO 7380, A2 stainless, black: round 16) on black nylon washers, the back to the inserts in its land strips: 16 (M5 x 40 into HDPE, M5 x 30 into plywood); in the Cloud from round 36 22 x M5 x 30, 18 round the edge and 4 into the braces' bosses (the cord seal leaves no gasket under the back)

levelling-feet.model: Levelling feet M8, a 40 mm swivel base on a rubber pad, black, with lock nuts, a set of 4

levelling-feet-black.model: Levelling feet M8, all black: the stem and its M8 jam nut (13 across flats, 5 thick) black oxide, a 40 mm swivel base in black, a satin black NBR pad, a set of 4 (the detail pass, 2026-11-12: no bright metal under the cabinet)

back-screws-flush.model: M5 x 30 countersunk socket heads (ISO 10642, A2 stainless, black), no washers, the back to the inserts in its land strips and the braces' bosses: 24, 20 round the edge evenly spaced and 4 into the bosses; each in a 90 degree countersink in the back, the head 0.1 under its face, torqued to 1.5 N m (the detail pass, 2026-11-12; were button heads)

rating-engraving.model: The rating plate's lines laser-engraved 0.1 deep in the back's outer face over the compartment's black flange (the maker, the product, the model and serial number, the ratings, where it was designed, the WEEE bin), on the cabinet shop's laser at the back's last operation: about 3 minutes a back (the detail pass, 2026-11-12: no separate plate, no screws)

m6-acrylic-inserts-low.model: M6 brass threaded inserts, knurled, bonded with epoxy into 8.5 holes in the acrylic panel, with M6 x 25 black ultra-low-head socket screws (a 13 across head 1.8 high, A2 black, wide enough to cover the woofer's slot) tightened to 5 N m; a set of 8 (the 15PR400's eight slots on 374). The detail pass, 2026-11-12: the heads cannot be flush, since the woofer's cast flange has slots, not countersinks

push-on-terminal-black.model: 6.3 mm fully insulated push-on terminal, black nylon boot (the woofer's and the HF driver's terminals capped black)

braid-sleeve.model: Black braided PET sleeve, expandable, 6 mm (the HF and IR leads, 3 m) and 10 mm (the woofer's lead, 1 m), with black heat-shrink at each end, a speaker

m5-inserts-plastic.model: M5 threaded inserts for plastics (self-tapping, brass), a set of 16, in 7.2 holes 12 deep in the back's HDPE land strips

m5-inserts-wood.model: M5 threaded inserts for wood (hex drive), a set of 16, in 8 holes 12 deep in the back's plywood cleats

m8-inserts-plastic.model: M8 threaded inserts for plastics (self-tapping, brass), a set of 4, in 11.5 holes 15 deep in the HDPE bottom, for the feet

m8-inserts-wood.model: M8 threaded inserts for wood (hex drive), a set of 4, in 12.5 holes 15 deep in the plywood bottom, for the feet

m6-acrylic-inserts.model: M6 brass threaded inserts, knurled, bonded with epoxy into 8.5 holes in the acrylic panel, with M6 x 25 button heads (A2-70) tightened to 5 N m, not 15: an A2-70 M6 yields near 9 N m, and the bonded insert is the weaker part (the engineering audit, 2026-11-01: make/engineering-audit.md); a set of 8 (the 15PR400's eight holes on 374)

acrylic-cement.model: Two-part polymerising acrylic cement for thick cast sheet (ACRIFIX 2R 0190 or Weld-On 40; round 35: not 1R 0192, a one-part cement that cures by light and will not cure through the deep tints), clear, about 0.5 kg a speaker: the corners, the braces, the ribs and the back's land strips

m5-inserts-acrylic.model: M5 brass threaded inserts, knurled, a set of 22 (16 before round 36), bonded with epoxy into 8 holes 12 deep in the back's acrylic land strips and the braces' four bosses

m8-inserts-acrylic.model: M8 brass threaded inserts, knurled, a set of 4, bonded with epoxy into 12.5 holes 15 deep in the acrylic bottom, for the feet

laser-etch.model: Laser etching into the cast acrylic, frosted, about 0.1 deep, from a vector file: as standard (round 24) EARF 140 wide high on the back, the etch filled with the speaker's own colour (a deeper tint of it, wiped in and cured)
laser-etch.supplier: a laser-cutting shop with an engraver

uv-print.model: UV flatbed print on the cast acrylic over a white underprint: round 24's option of the globe in its six colours and its outline in the front corner, about 50 across
uv-print.supplier: a sign or print shop with a UV flatbed printer

back-cord-seal.model: EPDM cord 4 mm, 60 Shore A, about 2.7 m, its ends vulcanised into a loop for the lands' groove (round 36: in place of the sponge gasket), and a spare
back-cord-seal.supplier: any seal supplier (O-ring cord and a splice kit)

hypex-remote-kit.model: Fusion Remote Kit H08U003549: an IR receiver PCBA with a bi-colour LED, a 5-pin cable 125 cm to J15 on the FA122's input board, two light pipes, a tinted perspex window and screws; in the master speaker only (Hypex: "This set must be used in master devices if the Hypex remote is to be used (remote not included)")
hypex-remote-kit.supplier: soundimports.eu (EUR 24.95 incl. VAT; hypex.nl shows prices after login only)

hypex-remote.model: Hypex Remote Control H08U001537, IR (Philips RC-5, device 16: power 50, volume up 51, down 52, mute 53), its CR2032 included; one a pair, not supplied with the amplifier

hypex-link-coax.model: 75 ohm coaxial cable with RCA plugs, 5 m (Hypex: under 25 m), the master FA122's S/PDIF I/O to the slave's: Hypex's link carries the volume and the remote's commands to the second speaker, whose own IR is disabled

ir-cable-kit.model: the Fusion Remote Kit's own 5-pin cable, 125 cm, to J15 on the FA122's input board (counted with the kit)

mains-cord-nema.model: Mains cord set, NEMA 5-15P to IEC 60320 C13, 2 m, 18 AWG SJT, black, UL listed (UL 817) (the engineering audit, 2026-11-01: make/engineering-audit.md): a listed cord is part of the end product's listing

plinth-led.model: REPLACED 2026-11-02 by the uplight (uplight-strip, uplight-panel; the owner: the light goes up through the speaker). COB LED strip, 24 V, 4.8 W/m, 2700 K, CRI 90+ (R9 > 50), dotless, 8 mm, 2.1 m a speaker in four lengths joined by short soldered jumpers at the corners (clear of the foot pads), in a shallow aluminium channel (about 10 x 4) with a frosted PMMA diffuser, bonded into a groove routed in the plinth's bottom frame 40 in from its edge (the owner, 2026-11-01: the plinth lit from underneath; the coordinator, 2026-11-01: the bare strip at 40 kept after the pool tests; variants/BASES.md)

plinth-channel.model: NOT IN THE LIST: the tested alternative (variants/BASES.md, Tested and not adopted). Black anodised aluminium U-channel, about 43 x 5 outside, 1.5 walls, cut and mitred to a 480 x 490 frame, carrying the strip and its 40 x 3 opal diffuser; light tight above and at the sides so no light enters the clear frame; held to the bottom frame's underside by M3 stainless screws into threaded inserts about every 250, not bonded, so the strip can be replaced (the coordinator, 2026-11-01; variants/BASES.md)

plinth-supply.model: Plug-in power supply, 24 V DC, 90 W (3.75 A; the uplight draws about 59 W at full with the 40 W centre panel, 2026-11-03; Class 2 at 24 V allows up to 100 VA), UL listed Class 2 (UL 1310) or IEC 62368-1 PS1, desktop or wall type, with a 2 m lead to the plinth's DC socket: separate from the FA122's mains (the owner, 2026-11-01: the plinth lit from underneath; variants/BASES.md)

uplight-strip.model: COB LED strip, 24 V, 10 W/m, 4000 K, CRI 90+ (R9 > 50), dotless, 8 mm, 1.84 m a speaker in four lengths (two of 360 under the sides' bottom edges, two of 480 under the front and back panels' edges, through the bottom panel they stand on), each in an aluminium U-channel (12 x 7) with a frosted PMMA lens, on nylon standoffs in a 16 x 8 groove in the plinth's top frame, clear of the acrylic all round (the owner, 2026-11-02: the light goes up through the speaker; variants/BASES.md)

uplight-channel.model: Aluminium U-channel, 12 x 7, 1.5 walls, black anodised, four lengths cut to the strips, each on three M3 nylon standoffs screwed into inserts in the groove's floor, so neither channel nor strip touches the acrylic (variants/BASES.md)

uplight-panel.model: The uplight's centre panel: an aluminium-core LED board, 24 V, 40 W (2026-11-03, from 16 W: the coordinator's next step toward the underlit look), 4000 K, CRI 90+, about 400 x 260, mid-power LEDs on a 20 mm grid, on a finned black anodised aluminium heat sink (a 3 mm plate with 15 mm fins down into the floor gap) on four glass-filled nylon brackets in the plinth's opening, none of it touching the acrylic, 8 under a 3 mm opal PMMA diffuser (420 x 280) held 10 under the cabinet's bottom; the plate vented round its edges (variants/BASES.md)

cabinet-wash.model: PROPOSAL (the cabinet wash, for the owner): COB LED strip, 24 V, 10 W/m, 4000 K, CRI 90+, 8 mm, 1.06 m a speaker in three lengths (two of 310 at the side walls' feet, one of 440 at the front panel's), bonded to the bottom panel's top face inside the cabinet between each wall and its lining, aimed up the wall; a 2-pin sealed connector (IP67, panel mount, potted) through the bottom panel at a foot pad mates with a spring contact in the plinth's top frame, so the cabinet lifts off its plinth with nothing to unplug (variants/BASES.md)

builtin-strip.model: PROPOSAL (the built-in light, for the owner, 2026-11-03): COB LED strip, 24 V, 4000 K, CRI 90+ (R9 > 50), dotless, 8 mm, 1.42 m a speaker (as rendered 2026-11-03: 15 W/m on the floor, 30 W/m on the brace, about 33 W) in five lengths (on the bottom panel: 440 behind the batt, under the back lining, and 110 behind each port; on the brace: two of 380), each in a black aluminium U-channel (12 x 7) with a frosted PMMA lens, aimed straight up, on three M3 nylon standoffs screwed into inserts bonded in the acrylic; each run on its own JST connector; fed from an external 24 V Class 2 / PS1 plug-in supply through a panel connector in the back's cable gland (variants/BASES.md)

builtin-standoffs.model: M3 nylon standoffs, 6 hex x 3, with M3 brass inserts bonded in the acrylic, fifteen a speaker (three a run of the built-in light)

reflector-film.model: PROPOSAL (2026-11-03): white diffuse reflector film, PET about 0.2 mm, adhesive backed, cut to the bottom panel's bare floor in each ports' bay (two pieces, about 160 x 335), so the light inside goes back up instead of down through the floor

plinth-controller.model: The plinth light's controller, in the plinth (2026-11-02: two channels for the uplight, the edge strips and the centre panel, balanced at the factory): a 24 V PWM dimmer (MOSFET, about 1 kHz above flicker limits or 20 kHz), its enable from the FA122's on/standby state through an opto-isolator (the state line to be confirmed with Hypex; else a switch on the plinth's back edge), four steps (off, 25, 50, 100 %) on a touch pad under the plinth's back edge, 50 % by default (the owner, 2026-11-01: the plinth lit from underneath; variants/BASES.md)
